pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/naming.rs:239 The one prompt this context assembles itself (the Haiku session-title fallback) cuts the task at 2,000 characters, possibly mid-sentence, and does not tell the model anything was dropped, so the model names a session from a partial task it takes to be the whole thing.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/naming.rs:239 The budget is counted in characters rather than tokens, the cut can fall mid-sentence, and the prompt carries no notice of what was removed. The technique asks for all three: a token count, a semantic boundary, and a notice.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/naming.rs:238 The task text comes from the caller or dispatcher, so it is not authored by the system, but it is interpolated raw after a colon with no fence or delimiter and no trust class declared. Instructions inside the task read as instructions to the namer.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/naming.rs:236 The prompt opens with the done shape (a 3-5 word Title Case tab label) instead of a role claim. Its negations sit beside a positive instruction, and clean_name strips quotes and punctuation anyway.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/naming.rs:235 This is a one-shot family with exactly one assembly site: no identity or policy layers, the task at the tail, and nothing appended after the format! returns. It is minimal, but there is no sprawl.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/pty.rs:37 This is the preserved-session regime: claude --resume keeps the conversation, so the wake sends a short delta prompt (orient in one line, then wait) rather than replaying the standing layers. It is sent only when resume_target finds a bound claude_session_id.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/registry.rs:2597 Claude Code holds the transcript (the agent-held regime). Fleet sends only new user turns as stream-json deltas and never edits or compacts the list itself. transcript_read.rs only reads counters.
